title: Does Weight Sparsity Improve Circuit Recoverability? Replicating OpenAI's Weight-Sparse Transformer Study on GPT-2

novelty_assessment.reasoning: OpenAI published 'Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits' (arXiv:2511.13653, Nov 2025), which directly trains weight-sparse GPT-2-style transformers and measures circuit recoverability across sparsity levels. The proposed study is essentially a replication of this existing work on the same model architecture (GPT-2) with the same methodology (attribution patching on IOI at multiple sparsity levels). The core question—does weight sparsity improve circuit recoverability—is answered by the existing paper, which finds circuits ~16x smaller at matched loss. A replication adds marginal value but the research question is largely addressed.

title: Attention Superposition in GPT-2: Quantifying Cross-Layer Attention Representations Using Probing

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Superposition and cross-layer entanglement are well-studied concepts (Anthropic's toy models, SAE work), and cross-layer probing has been explored in various forms. However, the specific approach of systematically training pairwise linear probes between all attention head Q/K/V outputs across layers to quantify the degree of cross-layer attention entanglement has not been directly published. Related work exists on layer-wise feature entanglement (e.g., features expanding and entangling with depth) but the specific probe-based quantification methodology for attention heads is a partial contribution.

citation_verification.detail: Elhage et al. 'Toy Models of Superposition' (2022) and subsequent SAE work cover superposition broadly. Layer-wise analysis exists but not with this specific pairwise probing methodology for attention heads.

title: Varying the Faithfulness Metric in Circuit Evaluation: Does Choice of Ablation Type Change Which Circuit Is Found Best?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Chughtai et al., 'Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics Are Not Robust' (arXiv:2407.08734, COLM 2024) directly addresses this question. They show that existing faithfulness metrics are highly sensitive to ablation methodology (zero, mean, resample), with resample ablations producing systematically lower faithfulness than mean ablations (p=1e-5). The proposed 3x2 confusion matrix of cross-metric faithfulness on IOI is a subset of what this published paper already demonstrates. Additionally, Li & Janson, 'Optimal ablation for interpretability' (arXiv:2409.09951) further extends this line of work.

title: SAE Features for Code vs Natural Language: Are Code-Specific Features More Monosemantic?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: While SAE monosemanticity has been studied extensively for natural language and for vision-language models (arXiv:2504.02821), and SAE features have been applied to code models, the specific controlled comparison—training matched SAEs on the same model with code vs natural language corpora and comparing monosemanticity metrics—has not been directly published. Cross-modal SAE comparisons exist (vision vs language) but not the code vs natural language comparison with matched hyperparameters on the same base model. This is a genuine gap.

title: Toy Model Superposition Under Correlated Inputs: Does Feature Correlation Change the Packing Geometry?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Anthropic's 'Toy Models of Superposition' (Elhage et al., 2022) already explores correlated and anti-correlated features, finding that correlated features tend toward orthogonal representations while anti-correlated features can share directions. The paper explicitly discusses how feature correlation affects superposition geometry. Additionally, 'Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry' (arXiv:2602.02224, Feb 2026) provides further theoretical treatment. The core question is partially addressed by the original paper's section on correlated features, though a more systematic parameter sweep over correlation strength could add incremental value.

title: MIB Causal Variable Localization: Does SAE Dictionary Size Affect DAS Probe Accuracy?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The MIB benchmark (Mueller et al., arXiv:2504.13151, ICML 2025) already evaluates SAEs against DAS in the causal variable localization track, finding that SAE features are not better than neurons and are high-variance. However, the specific question of how SAE dictionary size affects DAS probe accuracy was not systematically varied in the MIB paper—they used fixed SAE configurations. A dictionary size sweep is a natural extension but the broader finding (SAEs underperform DAS) is already established.

title: Circuit Overlap Between Related Tasks: How Much Do the IOI and Greater-Than Circuits Share?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Merullo et al., 'Circuit Component Reuse Across Tasks in Transformer Language Models' (ICLR 2024) directly studies circuit overlap in GPT-2, finding ~78% overlap in attention heads between IOI and Colored Objects circuits. While the proposed study specifically compares IOI with Greater-Than (rather than Colored Objects), the methodology and core question of cross-task circuit overlap in GPT-2 is thoroughly addressed. The Greater-Than circuit has also been independently studied (Hanna et al.). The proposed work would be an incremental extension to a different task pair.

title: Stress-Testing Attribution Graphs With Counterfactual Prompts: How Stable Are Discovered Circuits?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The instability of circuit discovery methods is documented: 'Mechanistic Interpretability as Statistical Estimation: A Variance Analysis' (arXiv:2510.00845) shows high variability in edge importance depending on input-counterfactual pairs, with low signal-to-noise ratios. Chughtai et al. (COLM 2024) shows metric sensitivity. However, these works focus on traditional circuit discovery (ACDC, attribution patching), not specifically on Anthropic's attribution graphs from circuit tracing. The specific stress-test of attribution graph stability under prompt variations is a partially novel application to the newer methodology, though the general finding of instability is well-established.

title: How many tokens deep is alignment across model families? A comparative audit

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Qi et al., 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' (arXiv:2406.05946, ICLR 2025 Outstanding Paper) established the shallow alignment phenomenon and measured KL divergence between base and aligned models. Follow-up work includes 'Any-Depth Alignment' (arXiv:2510.18081) and 'Safety Alignment Depth: A Markov Chain Perspective' (arXiv:2502.00669). However, a systematic comparative audit across 4-5 model families (Llama, Gemma, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) using alignment depth curves with a standardized metric has not been the focus of a single paper—existing work tends to use 1-2 model families. The comparative angle adds value.

title: Does alignment depth correlate with prefilling attack success rate across models?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) established shallow alignment and discussed prefilling attacks as one exploitation vector, but did not systematically measure the correlation between alignment depth (as a continuous metric) and prefilling attack success rate (ASR) across multiple model families. AdaPPA (arXiv:2409.07503) studies adaptive prefilling attacks but does not correlate with alignment depth measurements. The specific hypothesis—that alignment depth predicts prefilling ASR as a cheap safety proxy—is a novel empirical contribution that connects two established research directions with a clear, testable prediction.
